items.claim: The single_saying call for 10:14 is well-grounded and its continuation-paragraph fold disclosure is accurate.
items.evidence: Both spliced Hebrew quotes byte-match oshb:Eccl.10.14 (tier: byte). The WEB verse folds internally across its own paragraph mark, between “multiplies words.” and “Man doesn't know what will be” (web:Eccl.10.14) — one of exactly 2 book-wide continuation-fold sites (web:Eccl.7.8, web:Eccl.10.14) — and the row's two WEB quotes each sit wholly on one side of that internal mark rather than bridging it, so the fold's verbatim hazard is correctly navigated rather than tripped. The rejected alternative (clustering with 10:12-13 on "words"/fool vocabulary) correctly distinguishes the construct phrase "words of the mouth" in vv.12-13 from v.14's own bare verb-object construction, and the sentence-zone single_saying default (9:17-10:20) governs.
tier_citations: tier-4 metadata: continuation-fold inventory, 2 book-wide sites

items.claim: The single_saying call for 10:15 is well-grounded; its rejection of clustering with 10:14 on the shared not-knowing motif is correctly argued from construction, not theme.
items.evidence: The spliced Hebrew byte-matches oshb:Eccl.10.15 (tier: byte). Both v.14 and v.15 open with a form of the root ידע ("not know"), a real shared root the row explicitly names, and it correctly treats this as thematic texture rather than a shared construction — different conjugation, different negated object (unknowable future vs. the way to town) — which clears the cross-seam-cohesion bar without over-claiming a cluster.

items.claim: The saying_cluster call for 10:16-17 rests on a verified byte-true repeated construct phrase, but the row's observed_substrate_signals miscite the melekh_sites inventory object as covering 10:16-17, which it does not.
items.evidence: Direct byte check confirms the repeated phrase אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ ("land, that-your-king") is identical across oshb:Eccl.10.16 and oshb:Eccl.10.17 (tier: byte), a genuine 2-shared-content-token construction run that clears the cluster-cohesion bar — that part of the row stands. However, the cited "melekh_sites" device-inventory object (its own count_object restricted to מלך with article/prefix forms) lists only Eccl.1.1, 1.12, 2.12, 4.14, 5.8, 8.2, 8.4, 9.14, 10.20 — NOT 10.16 or 10.17. A book-wide contiguous-skeleton sweep for the bare root מלך independently confirms this: it returns 11 verses and likewise excludes 10.16/10.17, because שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ carries a non-final כ before the attached 2ms suffix ך rather than the free word's final ך — the final-letter-allography trap. Citing "melekh_sites (royal vocabulary shared with the chapter-closing verse)" for this row therefore names an inventory object whose own verse list does not contain either cited verse.
tier_citations: sweep: מלך contiguous skeleton, 11 verses, excludes 10.16/10.17

items.claim: single_saying for 10:18 is well-grounded; the rejected alternative correctly identifies the lexical break with 10:19.
items.evidence: The spliced Hebrew byte-matches oshb:Eccl.10.18 (tier: byte). No lexeme is reused between 10:18 (roof/house/slothfulness vocabulary) and 10:19 (feast/wine/money vocabulary), which the row correctly names in rejecting a household-theme cluster; the sentence-zone single_saying default applies.

items.claim: single_saying for 10:19 is well-grounded; the WEB quotes are verbatim and the rejected alternative correctly separates this verse from the preceding royal oracle.
items.evidence: The spliced Hebrew byte-matches oshb:Eccl.10.19 (tier: byte); both WEB quotes (“A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad” / “money is the answer for all things”) are verbatim against web:Eccl.10.19. No lexeme is shared with the אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ oracle of 10:16-17, supporting the row's own rejection of that alternative.

items.claim: single_saying for 10:20 is well-grounded; both the ketiv/qere disclosure and the melekh_sites citation are byte-accurate, and the admonition_unit rival is properly engaged and rejected.
items.evidence: MT 10:20 is a genuine ketiv/qere verse (pmarks kq inventory, single-witness disclosed) with the inline unpointed ketiv הכנפים immediately preceding the pointed qere כְּנָפַ֖יִם, matching the row's claim (tier: byte). 10:20 is also a genuine member of the melekh_sites inventory (unlike 10:16-17 in the neighboring cluster row), so this row's citation of that object is accurate. The row correctly engages the real rival category (admonition_unit, which the operative-category rule permits anywhere with a one-sentence deviation disclosure) and rejects it on the sound ground that the warning is confined to one grammatical sentence rather than a multi-verse counsel block.

items.claim: The admonition_unit call for 11:1-2 is defensible on its own bytes, but its strongest_rejected_alternative is a strawman: it never engages the real rival of uniting 11:1-6 into one admonition_unit, which the book strategy itself names as the candidate span.
items.evidence: The spliced Hebrew quotes byte-match oshb:Eccl.11.1 and oshb:Eccl.11.2 (tier: byte). The row's only rejected alternative addresses splitting v.1 from v.2 — a rival no serious reading would propose given their shared imperative-plus-rationale structure. The real rival goes unaddressed: the imperative frame recurs at 11:6 (זְרַ֣ע/אַל תַּנַּ֣ח), bracketing the intervening gnomic observations of 11:3-5, and this row's own negated-knowledge clause (לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע, closing v.2) recurs twice more at 11:5 and once more at 11:6 — a continuous three-site epistemic refrain running across the full 11:1-6 span, not confined to this row's two verses. The neighboring row's own device_notes independently discloses this cross-row refrain continuing from v.2 into v.5-6, which sharpens rather than resolves the question of why 11:1-2 and 11:3-6 stand as two admonition_units instead of one.

items.claim: The admonition_unit call for 11:3-6 is internally coherent and its refrain quotes are byte-accurate, but (a) its rejected_alternative is a strawman that never engages uniting with 11:1-2 into one 11:1-6 admonition_unit, and (b) its observed_substrate_signals miscite reut_ruach/rayon_ruach, idiomatic "chasing/grasping wind" phrases that do not occur anywhere in this row's span.
items.evidence: The negated-knowledge quotes byte-match oshb:Eccl.11.5 (two occurrences) and oshb:Eccl.11.6 (tier: byte). On (a): the row's rejected alternative considers only splitting the two v.5 occurrences apart, not the real rival of merging backward with 11:1-2, despite the row's own rationale naming that the refrain "is introduced one verse earlier at" Eccl.11.2 and continues here — an argument at least as strong for unity as for division — and the book strategy itself names 11:1-6, not two sub-spans, as the admonition_unit candidate bounded by the imperative/jussive frames. On (b): a direct skeleton sweep for the phrase רעות רוח returns only Eccl.1.14, 2.11, 2.17, 2.26, 4.4, 4.6, 6.9, and for רעיון רוח only Eccl.1.17, 4.16 — neither list includes any verse in this row's 11.3-11.6 span. The only רוח tokens in this span (11:4 שֹׁמֵ֥ר ר֖וּחַ, 11:5 דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָר֔וּחַ) carry the bare, literal sense (observing/way of the wind), not the idiomatic vanity formula the cited inventory objects track — the resh-ayin-family conflation the shared hazard catalog warns against.

sweep: רעיון רוח skeleton, 2 verses, excludes 11.3-11.6
